replacements.section_heading: Follow instruments before construction
replacements.original_text: The next chronology should distinguish acceptance of each condition from introduction or enactment of the amendments. A permit, site servicing, construction start, completion and occupancy would follow their own documentary trail. Readers should also retain the exact application number when searching, because an address or nearby project can lead to a different file. This discipline makes the remaining work understandable: a favorable planning decision changes permission, while the project still needs the instruments and practical arrangements that allow building to proceed.
replacements.replacement_text: The next chronology should distinguish acceptance of each condition from introduction or enactment of the amendments. A permit, site servicing, construction start, completion and occupancy would follow their own documentary trail. Readers should also retain the exact application number when searching, because an address or nearby project can lead to a different file. Council adoption records a planning decision subject to the stated conditions; it does not by itself establish that the withheld amendments have been enacted or that a building permit has been issued.
replacements.reason: Replace the shorthand that adoption changes permission with the narrower distinction supported by Council decision part 8.

replacements.section_heading: Read the project results within their design
replacements.original_text: ARENA's final and retrospective materials describe the project and reported results. They can support an account of the demonstrated functions and the conditions under which they were examined. They are not an independent estimate of what customer reliability would have been without the project. A reader should identify the reporting period, event or operating mode and the source of each measure. This keeps the demonstration useful while preserving the difference between a project report and a causal evaluation of broader public benefit.

It identifies the exact documentary joins needed for a reliable authorization-to-mission account.

replacements.section_heading: What each instrument contributes
replacements.original_text: The Golden-Mars material identifies an SCC decision and a route condition. It does not establish final land arrangements, completed construction or energization. The GS-5 order defines a large-load rate class and risk-allocation rules with a later effective date in the inherited record. It does not identify a particular customer's capacity or consumption. A regional account should explain both instruments while preserving their separate recipients, obligations and timelines. That makes the connection between infrastructure planning and commercial service intelligible without merging their stages.
replacements.replacement_text: The SCC's June 29, 2026 Final Order in PUR-2025-00056 approves Route 3A, incorporates its April 9 order and specifies a subsequent map/CPCN process. The July 20 order declines to suspend that decision; it does not cancel the transmission approval. The official docket checked September 22 lists Under Appeal. That docket field is not an appellate merits ruling or confirmation of unrestricted construction authority. Separately, the SCC's November 25, 2025 announcement reports approval of GS-5 with effect from January 1, 2027. This check covered the announcement, not the full rate order or later amendments. The records do not establish land-right completion, energization, customer eligibility or actual billing.
replacements.reason: Replace a general-information citation and ambiguous future-decision wording with located, separately dated artifacts and their inspection limits.

replacements.section_heading: What to examine next
replacements.original_text: A final route or land record would clarify the infrastructure path; an inspection or energization record would demonstrate a later physical event. A named GS-5 service agreement or customer operating return would illuminate a different part of the chain. Any claim about costs borne by other customers would need the relevant tariff and accounting evidence. The September case preserves those questions as separate next steps and offers no capacity, reliability or affordability outcome for the corridor as a whole.
replacements.replacement_text: The June route order is now located; the remaining legal review concerns the incorporated April conditions, map/CPCN compliance, land rights and later court or appellate orders. For GS-5, inspect the full tariff, applicable amendments and customer-specific documents before drawing eligibility, billing or cost-allocation conclusions. The separate October 1 Loudoun standards appointment is unchanged. No corridor-wide capacity, reliability or affordability outcome follows from this correction.

replacements.section_heading: A canceled project is not a complete company diagnosis
replacements.original_text: The expansion record does not establish why that project stopped, whether another expansion occurred or what happened to output and employment afterward. The report should preserve the named project and event rather than infer a company-wide decline. It should also avoid using a later capability statement to erase the earlier cancellation. The two sources can coexist in a chronology while answering different questions. That is a more faithful treatment of industrial development than assigning a broad adverse-event label from one incomplete strand.

Its proposed expansion is not a completion report. The page supplies no status-effective date or reason, and does not establish cancellation of every physical expansion. Zero grant disbursement is not zero private investment. Neither this administrative record nor a later capability statement establishes subsequent output, employment or company-wide decline.
replacements.reason: Name the exact administrative project and preserve its combined label, funding boundary and missing causal/operating evidence.

replacements.original_text: The inherited Golden-Mars and GS-5 case contains two concrete decisions. Virginia approved a future large-load rate class, scheduled to become effective January 1, 2027, and conditionally approved a transmission project with a local route dependency. The first concerns the terms under which a class of customers would be served. The second concerns authority for a physical transmission proposal. Their proximity does not make them one customer delivery event.

replacements.section_heading: Northern Virginia shows the institutional handoffs
replacements.replacement_text: The route order is located; the remaining questions concern its incorporated April conditions, map/CPCN compliance, land rights and any later court or appellate orders. Those matters were not fully inspected in the retained check. Construction, inspection, energization and a named service arrangement require their own records. For GS-5, the full tariff, applicable amendments and customer documents remain necessary before an eligibility or billing conclusion. Resolving one procedural question does not close the physical service or customer-acceptance gap.
replacements.reason: Replace the still-missing-final-route framing with the unverified compliance, court, land, physical-delivery and customer-specific questions.
replacements.original_text: The next useful questions therefore concern final routing, land rights, construction, inspection and energization, followed by an identifiable customer agreement. Those are distinct documents with different responsible parties. A regulatory approval can resolve an institutional dependency while leaving the physical service dependency open.

For Arizona, the decisive additions remain facility-specific utility acceptance and operating measurements. Repeated reporting should retain the same building or fab identity, measurement period, units, configuration and exception treatment so readers can distinguish a new measurement from a changed definition.
replacements.reason: Retire the resolved request to locate a final route order without claiming that the downstream evidence has been obtained or changing the Arizona boundary.

replacements.section_heading: Admit a measure only within its definition
replacements.original_text: A numerical observation needs its unit, denominator, geography, period, method and revision lineage. An EIA nameplate-capacity record cannot establish availability; a queue entry cannot establish a completed plant. NERC planning submissions and LBNL scenarios have their own forward-looking meanings. These inherited examples show why the label on a quantity matters as much as the quantity itself. Missing outcome fields remain missing. A calculated value should be added only when the inputs describe compatible objects and the calculation preserves their limitations.

The latter study separately estimates historical electricity use and is distinct from LBNL's queue report. These examples show why the label on a quantity matters as much as the quantity itself. Missing outcome fields remain missing. A calculated value should be added only when the inputs describe compatible objects and the calculation preserves their limitations.

replacements.section_heading: Use operating comparators without transferring their results
replacements.original_text: The inherited Chandler material provides an operating municipal and industrial comparison. It can help readers understand how reclaimed-water infrastructure and reporting may be organized. It cannot establish Phoenix project-specific performance, because provider systems, customers and measurement boundaries differ. A defensible comparison should identify what is actually shared: perhaps a reporting concept or a treatment function, rather than an outcome value. The report should retain operator attribution and avoid treating a successful arrangement in one place as proof that another planned system has achieved the same result.
replacements.replacement_text: The City of Chandler describes a reclaimed-water network serving municipal and other users, with reuse that includes industrial use and aquifer recharge. Its public system account provides a comparison of how treatment and distribution are organized, not a customer-level industrial operating record. It does not establish Phoenix project-specific performance: providers, customers and measurement boundaries differ. A defensible comparison identifies a shared treatment or reporting function without transferring one system's stated outcomes to another. Metered industrial flows, reliability and facility balances still require their own records.
replacements.reason: Add the exact municipal source and limit the comparison to attributed system organization, retaining provider and measurement boundaries.

replacements.section_heading: Keep observation, forecast and scenario distinct
replacements.original_text: NOAA's global reporting describes broad conditions over stated periods, while ENSO discussions provide probabilistic outlooks. Historical station observations answer a more local question, but station moves, missing values and quality flags can affect interpretation. A forecast issued on one date is not an observation of what later happened. A useful account should identify which kind of product it uses, when the information was available and the period it describes. This makes it possible to evaluate the decision without granting its authors knowledge they did not have at the time.
replacements.replacement_text: NOAA NCEI's January 14, 2026 summary of the 2025 Global Climate Report describes retrospective global conditions for calendar 2025; its December section has a separate monthly scope. ENSO discussions, by contrast, provide probabilistic outlooks. Historical station observations answer a more local question, but station moves, missing values and quality flags can affect interpretation. A forecast issued on one date is not an observation of what later happened. A useful account should identify which kind of product it uses, when the information was available and the period it describes. This makes it possible to evaluate the decision without granting its authors knowledge they did not have at the time.

replacements.section_heading: Receiving-party evidence strengthens a delivery claim
replacements.original_text: The Advanced Manufacturing topic includes a named F-15EX receipt by a receiving wing, alongside other production and delivery records. A receiver-linked record is useful because it identifies where an asset entered a real operating organization. It remains narrower than a claim about fleet readiness, mission availability or sustained production cadence.
replacements.replacement_text: The Advanced Manufacturing topic includes a named F-15EX arrival at a receiving wing, alongside other production and delivery records. The wing's video-page description identifies EX16 and a December 11, 2025 receipt, while the page is dated February 17, 2026. This is receiving-unit arrival evidence, not a formal contractual acceptance date, fleet-readiness finding or complete production series. The separately retained September 22 failed-access finding concerns another Air Force production page; it neither verifies nor contradicts this wing account. An identity-linked acceptance ledger and compatible repeated observations are still required.
replacements.reason: Preserve the receiving-unit account and distinct event/publication dates without converting arrival or a different source access failure into formal acceptance or a recurring series.
